arguments.title: Synchformer: Efficient Synchronization from Sparse Cues
key_claims: A model trained for natural audiovisual events predicts offset from sparse short segments and separately considers whether a clip can be synchronized at all. This informs a transfer-check design, not a primary stage-light score: abstract illumination is not necessarily a visible physical sound source. Require known shifts, metronome/rate-matched and donor controls before any use. Do not infer designed appearance or genuine music conditioning from an unqualified synchronization model.

Verified full PDF SHA256 aeccfb5ddab382684792e3bb7c6ac99e56579f47f2a677b1d7f55784730cdf73. Read scope: Abstract; segment-level architecture/multimodal pretraining Sec3; offset/synchronizability evaluation discussion. Published evidence is outside LightSem; application here is a hypothesis.
